name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by nine points and has recently voted well left of that
Jacqui Irwin holds a large cash and outside-spending edge; Sam Gallucci has about $19,000 on hand
Open seat removes the incumbent cushion, but both nominees are non-incumbents in a D-held district
Prediction markets price Democratic odds around 95 percent
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's Democratic lean, a favorable recent voting record, and a decisive resource gap, with Irwin heavily funded and Gallucci nearly out of cash. The open seat and absence of polling add uncertainty, but not enough to move the race out of Safe D.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or new polling showing a single-digit race would warrant revisiting the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District, anchored in Ventura County, is open after Julia Brownley's retirement. The seat leans Democratic by about nine points on partisan fundamentals, and recent election results have run even more Democratic than that. Jacqui Irwin enters as the Democratic nominee with a large financial advantage, while Republican Sam Gallucci has spent down to roughly nineteen thousand dollars on hand.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing, which puts Democratic odds near ninety-five percent. The open-seat dynamic removes the incumbent's usual cushion, but the district's lean and the stark money gap point to Democrats as clear favorites in this Ventura County seat.
